blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: While the Platonic Representation Hypothesis posits that vision and language models converge toward compatible latent geometries, recovering class-level correspondences between unpaired modalities without cross-modal supervision remains challenging. Existing relational matching methods compare within-modality similarity kernels directly, although the same semantic structure may be represented through different numerical parameterizations across modalities. We propose RankAlign, a rank-based normalization strategy for class-level unpaired vision-language matching. RankAlign transforms each within-modality similarity kernel into an ordinal relational representation before permutation matching, while leaving the correspondence space and matching solver unchanged. The resulting representation is invariant to strictly increasing reparameterizations of similarity values while preserving the ordinal structure used for matching. We provide exact-recovery and stability guarantees that characterize correspondence recovery under both exact and partial ordinal agreement. Experiments across diverse frozen vision and language encoders and multiple datasets demonstrate improved and more stable class-level correspondence recovery, including under label corruption and domain shift.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: Recent advances in foundation models have fundamentally redefined representation learning across diverse modalities. While self-supervised vision encoders like DINO [ 1 ] and large-scale language models [ 3 , 17 ] have matured within their respective domains, multimodal contrastive frameworks such as CLIP [ 15 ] and SigLIP2 [ 22 ] have further bridged the two modalities. These architectures induce sophisticated latent representations that capture intricate structural and semantic nuances. Yet, despite this progress, the geometric alignment between visual and language representation spaces remains poorly understood when encoders are trained independently on disparate datasets. This poses a significant challenge for class-level unpaired cross-modal matching, where category structure is available within each modality, while the correspondence between visual and textual categories remains unknown and must be recovered.
blocks.zh: 基础模式最近的进展从根本上重新界定了不同方式的代表学习。 虽然DINO[1]等自我监督的视觉编码器和大规模语言模型[3,17]在各自的领域内已经成熟,但CLIP[15]和SigLIP2[22]等多模式对比框架进一步将这两种模式相通. 这些架构诱发了复杂的潜在表述,捕捉了复杂的结构和语义细微差别. 然而,尽管取得了这一进展,但当编码器在不同的数据集上接受独立培训时,视觉和语言代表空间之间的几何校正仍然不易理解。 这对类级无标跨模式匹配构成重大挑战,在每种模式内都有类别结构,而视觉类和文字类之间的对应关系仍然未知,必须收回.

blocks.en: Representation similarity and the Platonic hypothesis. Independently trained visual and language models frequently exhibit a striking convergence toward compatible representational structures. This phenomenon is formalized by the Platonic Representation Hypothesis, which posits that scaling and data diversity drive neural networks toward shared latent geometries that encode the statistical regularities of the world [ 6 ] . In vision-language settings, visual and textual encoders learn compatible relational structures despite disparate training objectives [ 10 , 19 ] . Although methods such as CCA [ 5 ] , SVCCA [ 16 ] , and CKA [ 8 ] provide quantitative measures of representational similarity, they rely on direct numerical comparisons that are inherently sensitive to modality-specific scale distortions and biases.
blocks.zh: 代表性相似性和柏拉图假说. 接受过独立培训的视觉和语言模型经常显示出对兼容的代表结构的显著一致。 这种现象由Platonic Presentation Hypothesis正式形成,它假定,扩大和数据多样性将神经网络推向共享的潜在地理学,以编码世界的统计规律[6]。 在视觉语言环境中,视觉和文字编码器学习兼容的关系结构,尽管培训目标各不相同[10、19]。 虽然CCA[5]、SVCCA[16]和CKA[8]等方法对代表性相似性提供了定量衡量,但它们依靠直接的数字比较,而这些比较对模式特有的比额表扭曲和偏差具有内在敏感性。

blocks.en:
Class-level unpaired vision-language matching. The emergence of a shared embedding space raises the fundamental question: can explicit correspondences between vision and language representations be recovered when independently trained encoders receive no paired supervision?
Traditional alignment relies on image–caption pairs or manually verified correspondences to learn a cross-modal mapping.
We instead study class-level unpaired vision-language matching with known within-modality groups and an unordered candidate set of textual concepts, where visual groups and a set of candidate textual concepts are available but their cross-modal correspondence is unknown.
Supervision is confined to constructing class-level representations within each modality, with no paired image–text samples, cross-modal anchors, or verified correspondences provided to the matching procedure. When reliable cross-modal anchors are available, supervised alignment is often simpler and more practical.
Our goal is to determine whether independently trained encoders contain sufficient relational structure to recover correspondence without such anchors. This zero-anchor setting can arise when visual groups and a candidate textual ontology are collected or maintained independently, so that both sides are available but their correspondence has not been verified. In this regime, correspondence recovery can reduce the need for manually established cross-modal anchors and also serves as a diagnostic of structural compatibility between independently trained representation spaces. More broadly, it tests whether cross-modal correspondence can emerge from relational structure alone, without shared training data or explicit cross-modal supervision.
Recent work frames this problem as matching pairwise relationships between embeddings [ 19 ] . Such formulations arise naturally in kernel alignment [ 2 ] , graph matching via quadratic assignment [ 23 ] , and structural optimal transport, most notably the Gromov-Wasserstein ( 𝒢 ​ 𝒲 \mathcal{GW} ) distance [ 14 , 24 ] .

Instead of matching kernels based on raw values, we align them by comparing their rank-based transformation, which uses the ordering induced by these entries. The correspondence problem itself remains unchanged, while the matching signal is determined by relational order rather than raw kernel values.

Contributions. We study class-level unpaired vision-language matching with known
categories. Class-level representations are available
within each modality, while their cross-modal correspondence is unknown.
Our contributions are summarized as follows: • Solver-agnostic ordinal relational representation. We introduce a rank-based representation that plugs into existing blind-matching objectives and QAP solvers without changing the correspondence space or optimization procedure. RankAlign removes arbitrary strictly increasing reparameterizations of similarity values while retaining the ordinal structure used for matching. • Theory of ordinal correspondence recovery. We formalize cross-modal agreement up to modality-specific monotone reparameterizations and show that the resulting ordinal representation is invariant to such distortions. We further provide exact-recovery and stability guarantees that separate cross-modal ordinal disagreement from the intrinsic distinguishability of class relational profiles. • Empirical validation. Experiments across diverse vision and language encoders and datasets demonstrate that RankAlign achieves more stable and reliable cross-modal correspondence alignment.

blocks.en:
We measured performance using matching accuracy, defined as the fraction of correctly recovered class correspondences. A matching
accuracy of 1.00 1.00 corresponds to exact recovery of the ground-truth class permutation.
We compared against BlindMatch [ 19 ] using both Gromov–Wasserstein (( 𝒢 ​ 𝒲 \mathcal{GW} )) and Mutual kNN. RankAlign uses the same permutation solvers as the baselines but replaces the raw within-modality similarity kernels with the ordinal representation defined in Section 2.3 before matching.
To isolate the contribution of this representation, we additionally compare against z-score normalization, quantile normalization, and row-wise ranking under an identical protocol.
The controlled ablation in Appendix B.2 shows that the gains cannot be explained by generic normalization or local ranking alone. All experiments were conducted on a single NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU with 48GB memory.

blocks.en: Pre-trained models . We evaluated RankAlign using a variety of frozen pre-trained visual and textual encoders to cover diverse representation geometries and supervision paradigms, including DINO/DINOv2 [ 1 , 13 ] , DeiT [ 21 ] , and vision-language models such as CLIP [ 15 ] , SigLIP [ 25 ] , and SigLIP2 [ 22 ] . For language side, we primarily used SentenceTransformers models [ 17 ] .

blocks.en:
Prompt construction. Given an image classification dataset with N N visual groups, we form class-level prototypes independently in the two modalities. On the visual side, each image is embedded with the frozen visual encoder and the embeddings are averaged within each visual group. On the language side, we construct an unordered candidate set of N N textual concepts. For each candidate concept, we generate a small collection of semantically equivalent textual descriptions, embed them with the frozen language encoder, and average them to obtain a textual prototype. The correspondence between the visual groups and textual prototypes is withheld from the matching algorithm. The algorithm receives only the
two unordered sets of class-level prototypes and recovers their
cross-modal permutation from within-modality relational structure.

blocks.en: 4 Conclusions
blocks.zh: 4. 结论

blocks.en:
This work revisits class-level unpaired vision-language matching from an ordinal perspective and introduces RankAlign, a rank-based normalization strategy for relational correspondence. Rather than modifying the underlying permutation-matching framework, RankAlign changes the relational representation supplied to the matching objective. By emphasizing relational order over absolute similarity magnitudes, it provides a monotone-invariant signal for recovering cross-modal correspondences without cross-modal supervision. Beyond its empirical effectiveness, these findings offer strong support for the Platonic Representation Hypothesis, demonstrating that cross-modal convergence does not require rigid metric equivalence, but rather emerges naturally through shared relational topologies across independently trained representations.
A fundamental property of rank-based normalization lies in its complete invariance to strictly increasing reparameterizations, providing provable guarantees against modality-specific scale distortions, domain shifts, and monotonic noise. These theoretical properties translate directly into empirical robustness: across diverse frozen encoders and matching settings, RankAlign delivers stable class-level correspondence recovery even under severe corruption conditions. By formulating cross-modal correspondence in terms of relational order rather than absolute similarity magnitudes, the approach ensures invariant alignment without relying on cross-modal anchors or paired supervision.

This appendix provides proofs and additional details for the
theoretical results in the main text. We first establish the relation between relational distortion and agreement and prove the invariance properties of the rank representation. We then describe the full ordinal refinement used in the experiments. Next, we prove the exact-recovery and stability results and connect them to this refined representation and approximate solver outputs. Finally, we provide additional computational complexity details.

blocks.en: B.1 Datasets
blocks.zh: B.1 数据集

blocks.en: We evaluate RankAlign on diverse benchmarks spanning web-scale pseudo-label data, object recognition datasets at different semantic granularities, and a domain-specific medical imaging dataset.
blocks.zh: 我们评价RankAlign 的各种基准,包括网络尺度的伪标签数据、不同语义颗粒的物体识别数据集以及特定域的医学成像数据集。

blocks.en: CIFAR-100 and ImageNet-100. To study scalability, we evaluated the matching accuracy as a function of the number of classes N N using subsets of CIFAR-100 [ 9 ] and ImageNet-100 [ 18 ] . We varied N N across matching instances to assess performance under increasing task difficulty.
blocks.zh: CIFAR-100和图像网-100. 为了研究可扩展性,我们利用CIFAR-100[9]和ImageNet-100[18]的子集,评价了匹配精确度作为N类数量的一个函数. 在任务难度越来越大的情况下,我们使用不同的NN来评估业绩。

blocks.en: LAION pseudo-class dataset. We evaluated RankAlign on a pseudo-class dataset derived from the LAION-Aesthetic subset [ 20 ] . Since LAION lacks predefined class labels, we defined N = 20 N=20 visual categories and assign pseudo-labels via caption matching. To ensure label quality, we classified each image using both its original caption ( TEXT ) and a Moondream -generated auxiliary caption, retaining only samples with a unique, consistent top-scoring assignment. The dataset contains approximately 7,000 7{,}000 samples, with 200 200 – 500 500 images per class. Visual and language prototypes are constructed by averaging embeddings within each pseudo-class and its associated captions, respectively.
blocks.zh: LAION伪类数据集. 我们在LAION-美学子集产生的伪类数据集上评价了RankAlign [20]. 由于LAION缺乏预定义的类标签,我们定义了N=20N=20可视类,并通过标题匹配来指定伪标签. 为确保标签质量,我们使用原始字幕(TEXT)和由月梦生成的辅助字幕对每个图像进行分类,只保留具有独特、一致的上分任务的样本。 数据集包含约7000个7{,}000个样本,每类有200-500个图像. 视觉和语言原型通过平均嵌入每个伪类及其相关标题来构建.

blocks.en: Medical imaging dataset. We evaluated RankAlign on CheXpert [ 7 ] , a large-scale chest X-ray benchmark with 220,000 radiographs. We extracted a 12-class single-label subset by retaining samples with one positive finding, totaling about 62,000 images. This setting is challenging due to subtle inter-class differences, class imbalance, and the medical image-text domain gap.
blocks.zh: 医学成像数据集. 我们在CheXpert上评价了RankAlign[7],一个规模庞大的胸X射线基准,有22万幅放射图. 我们提取了一个12级的单标签子集 通过保留样本 并有一个肯定的发现, 总计约62 000个图像。 由于细微的阶级间差异,阶级失衡,以及医学影像-文字域间隙,这种设置具有挑战性.

blocks.en: B.2 Kernel Transformation Ablation
blocks.zh: B.2 内核转化

blocks.en: To determine whether the gains of RankAlign can be explained by generic normalization or by a single form of ranking, we conduct a controlled ablation on CIFAR-100. All variants use identical visual and language prototypes, class subsets, similarity kernels, encoders, and permutation solvers. Only the relational representation supplied to the solver is changed.
blocks.zh: 为了确定RankAlign的收益能否通过通用正常化或单一的排名形式来解释,我们对CIFAR-100进行了控制下消减. 所有变体都使用相同的视觉和语言原型,类子集,相似性内核,编码器,和通相解析器. 只有提供给解决者的关系代表被更改.

blocks.en:
We compare the raw kernel without transformation (none), z-score
normalization, row-wise ranking, quantile normalization, and the full RankAlign representation. Z-score normalization removes global mean and scale differences while preserving the relative spacing of kernel values. Row-wise ranking preserves local neighbor order but does not define a single kernel-level ordinal ordering. Quantile normalization aligns marginal value distributions.

blocks.en:
Table 5 shows that the improvement cannot be explained by normalization alone. Z-score normalization provides almost no gain over the raw value-based kernel, consistent with the fact that affine normalization does not alter the optimizer of the inner-product matching objective. Quantile normalization also yields limited improvements. Row-wise ranking performs substantially better than value-based normalization, confirming that local ordinal information is useful.
However, its advantage decreases as the problem size grows. RankAlign consistently achieves the highest matching accuracy across all problem sizes, indicating that the combination of kernel-level ordinal normalization and anchor-wise neighborhood order is more effective than generic normalization or local ranking alone.

然而,随着问题规模的扩大,其优势会减弱. RankAlign一贯实现所有问题大小的最高匹配精度,表明内核水平正统化和锚地相邻秩序的结合比一般正常化或仅局部排名更有效.

blocks.en: B.3 Comparison with Classical Structural Alignment Methods
blocks.zh: B.3 与古典结构调整方法的比较

blocks.en: To examine whether simpler classical alignment methods can recover the same cross-modal correspondence without RankAlign’s ordinal formulation, we compare against unsupervised Orthogonal Procrustes and standard entropic Gromov–Wasserstein optimal transport. All methods use the same class-level visual and language representations and are evaluated on the same CIFAR-100 matching instances, so the comparison isolates differences in the alignment objective rather than differences in the underlying encoders or prototypes.
blocks.zh: 为了检查更简单的古典式对接方法能否在没有RankAlign的正则配方的情况下恢复同样的交叉式对接,我们比较了无监督的正弦Procrustes和标准的Entropic Gromov-Wasserstein最佳运输方式. 所有方法都使用同级视觉和语言表现,并在同一CIFAR-100匹配实例上进行评估,因此比较隔离了对齐目标的差异而不是基础编码器或原型的差异.

blocks.en: Table 6: Comparison with classical structural alignment methods on CIFAR-100. All methods use the same class-level representations and matching instances. We report matching accuracy across problem sizes.
blocks.zh: 表6:与CIFAR-100上的经典结构对接方法的比较. 所有方法都使用同级的表示和相配实例. 我们报告问题大小的精确度

blocks.en: Table 6 shows that neither classical baseline approaches the performance of RankAlign across the evaluated backbones and problem sizes. Both Orthogonal Procrustes and vanilla GW-OT remain close to chance as N N increases, whereas RankAlign retains substantially higher matching accuracy. Because all methods operate on the same class-level representations, this difference cannot be attributed to stronger encoders or higher-quality prototypes. These results indicate that a global linear alignment or direct matching of the original metric structures is insufficient to recover the cross-modal correspondence in these experiments, and RankAlign is not replacing a comparably accurate simpler baseline.
blocks.zh: 表6显示,无论是传统的基线都无法接近RankAlign在评价的骨干和问题规模方面的业绩。 随着N N的增加,正弦蛋白和香草GW-OT仍然接近于机会,而RankAlign保留了相当高的匹配精度。 由于所有的方法都运行在同等级的表示上,这种差异不能归咎于更强大的编码器或更高质量的原型. 这些结果表明,全球线性对接或直接匹配原始的度量结构不足以恢复这些实验中的跨模式对应,而RankAlign并没有取代一个比较精确的更简单的基准.

blocks.en: In the main paper, we report representative larger-scale matching results for a subset of vision backbones to improve readability. We provide the full results across all evaluated backbones, including CLIP, DINOv2, DeiT, SigLIP, and SigLIP2.

blocks.en: B.5 Existing Assets and Licenses
blocks.zh: B.5 现有资产和许可证

blocks.en: This work uses existing public datasets and pretrained models, including LAION-Aesthetic, CIFAR-100, ImageNet-100, CheXpert, DINO/DINOv2, DeiT, CLIP, SigLIP/SigLIP2, and SentenceTransformers. We cite the original sources for these assets and use them only for research evaluation. We will follow the corresponding licenses and terms of use for each dataset and pretrained model, and will include detailed license information in the released code and supplemental documentation.
